Boil Plot for Zero-Inflated Gene Expression

Source: R/boilplot.R
do_BoilPlot.Rd

Creates boil plots for one or more genes from a Seurat object. Single-cell expression is dominated by zeros, which squash conventional violins towards the baseline. A boil plot separates the two questions a violin mixes together:

  • How many cells express the gene? A detection bar below zero shows the fraction of cells with non-zero expression (grey track = all cells, coloured fill = expressing cells, percentage label underneath).

  • How is the gene expressed in those cells? The violin, jittered points, centrality marker and optional boxplot (boxplot = TRUE) above zero use non-zero cells only.

Geometry and colours follow the original boil plot, drawn with BadranSeq's palette and theme_badranseq. For a single gene, returns a bare ggplot2 object. For multiple genes, returns a patchwork composition.

The boil plot design comes from the boilplot package by Lara Jerman (https://github.com/laraj1/boilplot-r, Python original at https://github.com/laraj1/boilplot-python). This function is a reimplementation in BadranSeq's visual style, with credit to the original as the source of inspiration.

Usage

do_BoilPlot(
  object,
  features,
  group.by = NULL,
  group.levels = NULL,
  layer = "data",
  assay = NULL,
  colors.use = NULL,
  min.nonzero = 10,
  pt.size = 0.7,
  pt.alpha = 0.6,
  jitter.width = 0.1,
  violin.alpha = 0.8,
  violin.width = 0.9,
  boxplot = FALSE,
  boxplot.width = 0.3,
  boxplot.alpha = 0.2,
  centrality = TRUE,
  centrality.fn = "median",
  ncol = 1,
  nrow = NULL
)

Arguments

object

Seurat object.

features

character. Gene names to plot (required). Metadata columns are not accepted; use do_ViolinPlot for those.

group.by

character. Metadata column for grouping. If NULL (default), uses active Idents.

group.levels

character. Subset of group levels to include, in the order given (default: NULL = all levels in their existing order).

layer

character. Layer to extract expression from (default: "data"). Use a non-negative layer such as "data" or "counts".

assay

character. Assay to use (default: NULL = DefaultAssay).

colors.use

character. Named vector of colors for groups. If NULL, generates colors automatically with generate_badranseq_colors.

min.nonzero

numeric. Minimum number of expressing cells a group needs to appear in a gene's panel (default: 10). Groups below the threshold are removed from that panel entirely, including their detection bar and x-axis position. Genes with no qualifying group are skipped with a warning.

pt.size

numeric. Jitter point size (default: 0.7).

pt.alpha

numeric. Jitter point transparency (default: 0.6).

jitter.width

numeric. Horizontal jitter width for points (default: 0.1).

violin.alpha

numeric. Violin fill alpha (default: 0.8).

violin.width

numeric. Maximum violin width (default: 0.9). All violins share this width regardless of group size, so small groups are not squashed.

boxplot

logical. Whether to overlay a boxplot (default: FALSE).

boxplot.width

numeric. Boxplot width (default: 0.3).

boxplot.alpha

numeric. Boxplot alpha (default: 0.2).

centrality

logical. Whether to show centrality point and label for non-zero cells (default: TRUE).

centrality.fn

character. Centrality function ("median" or "mean", default: "median").

ncol

numeric. Number of columns for patchwork layout when plotting multiple genes (default: 1, one gene per row so panels stack vertically).

nrow

numeric. Number of rows for patchwork layout (default: NULL = auto). Set ncol = NULL together with nrow to control rows only.

Value

A ggplot2 object (single gene) or patchwork object (multiple genes).

References

Jerman, L. boilplot: faithful and interpretable visualisations of zero-inflated distributions. https://github.com/laraj1/boilplot-r

See also

do_ViolinPlot, do_StatsViolinPlot

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(pbmc3k)

# Single gene
do_BoilPlot(pbmc3k, features = "CD8A", group.by = "seurat_annotations")

# Multiple genes, selected groups in a chosen order
do_BoilPlot(pbmc3k, features = c("GZMA", "NKG7", "PRF1"),
            group.by = "seurat_annotations",
            group.levels = c("NK", "CD8 T", "Memory CD4 T"))

# Mean instead of median, with boxplot overlay
do_BoilPlot(pbmc3k, features = "MS4A1", centrality.fn = "mean",
            boxplot = TRUE)
} # }
